audit.why: Win rate in the packet is 59.02% over 61 games and no elo-tier language appears in either layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart hands Kennen 6 of 7 stages while Zac wins the matchup 59.02%.
audit.why: A 59% matchup cannot have the loser leading six of seven stages. Kennen genuinely owns levels 1-3 (950-range Q, no melee answer), but from Levels 4-5 Zac's E cooldown drops from 21s to 15s and blob sustain matches the chip; by first item Zac eats a full Q rotation.
audit.corrected: Kennen / Kennen / Kennen / Skill / Skill / Zac / Zac.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere notes that Slicing Maelstrom has a flat 120s cooldown at all three ranks.
audit.why: Kennen's R never gets shorter with rank, while Zac's Let's Bounce! goes 120/105/90. From R2 onward Zac's ultimate is up more often than Kennen's, which is the whole reason the lane flips. A spent Slicing Maelstrom buys a full two minutes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers attribute the stun to Kennen's W ("W mark-stun", "Poke you with Q and W-stun") and the full layer says "Kennen wins by landing Lightning Rush".
audit.why: The stun is Mark of the Storm (P) and it requires three marks on the target. W (Electrical Surge) only applies a mark. Lightning Rush is not a "landed" ability at all - it is a movement form that applies a mark in passing. Framing the stun as a single ability makes players dodge the wrong thing: what you actually count is marks, not casts.
audit.corrected: Stun re-attributed to Mark of the Storm (P) at three stacks in whys[0], whys[1], spikes[0].text, wants.foe[0], early, and full enemyWin.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kennen.json (P "stuns enemies he hits 3 times with his abilities")

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood tells Zac to "W the %HP ticks" against Kennen.
audit.why: Unstable Matter deals a percentage of the TARGET's maximum health. Kennen is a squishy mage with the smallest health pool in this matchup, so W is Zac's weakest tool here, not part of the trade pattern. This same "W the %HP ticks" sentence is templated across many Zac matchups regardless of the enemy's health pool.
audit.corrected: full tradeGood rewritten to drop W from the pattern and say why.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (W "a percentage of their maximum health")

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention of Kennen's energy economy anywhere.
audit.why: Lightning Rush costs 80 energy - by far the most expensive spell in his kit (Q is 60 falling to 40, W is 40). A Kennen who has just spent Q and W frequently cannot afford his escape. That is a second, independent window on top of the 10/9/8/7/6 cooldown, and it is the one high-elo players actually bait.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kennen.json (E cost 80, Q cost 60/55/50/45/40, W cost 40)

audit.why: The existing guidance not to Slingshot in blind and to commit only once Lightning Rush is spent is sound; it just needed the real numbers attached, which the edits do.

Separately: the packet suspectName "Let's Bounce" is a FALSE POSITIVE across every Zac matchup - the on-disk text already reads "R (Let's Bounce!)" with the exclamation mark and the detector is stripping it. The three win[] edits change short enum-style labels ("Kennen" 6 chars -> "Skill" 5 / "Zac" 3) and will fall outside a literal +/-10% length band; they are the flagged level-chart defect and need the band waived for label fields, otherwise the reworded whys[3..5] will contradict the chart they explain.
